## The question

[The use of "tilde" changes the proximity to the set theory symbol (ref img)](https://tex.stackexchange.com/questions/12044/the-use-of-tilde-changes-the-proximity-to-the-set-theory-symbol-ref-img), asked by [Algific](https://tex.stackexchange.com/users/3796/algific) on TeX Stack Exchange (2011-02-25; [CC BY-SA 2.5](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/2.5/)):

> I just want to format a simple set theory example. But the following is annoying: 
>
> ```latex
> \documentclass{article}
> \begin{document}
> $A$$=$$(A \cup B)$
>
> $A \cap (( A) \cap B)$ $= $ $ A \cap \sim B$ 
> \end{document}
> ```
>
> [![image of example code][q-1]][q-1]
>
> See how close the cap gets to the 'A' because of the tilde sign? 
> I've used sim for the tilde sign. Any suggestions? 
>
>
>   [q-1]: FyLQbsQV.png
:::

Here is a complete code example with output (I just took Stefan's answer and wrote it out).

```latex
\documentclass{article}
\begin{document}
$A = (A \cup B)$

$A \cap (( A) \cap B) = A \cap \mathord{\sim}B$
\end{document}
```

![sample output][1]

  [1]: cSN9N.png

Switching in and out of math mode is not a good way to get extra spaces.  If you still want them after classifying the tilde as an ordinal, you can insert them with `\,`, `\; `, or `\ `.  See [Herbert's mathmode document](https://ctan.org/tex-archive/info/math/voss/mathmode/Mathmode.pdf) for FMTYEWTK.
